speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: asked	the Minister for Manpower (a) whether the Ministry is aware of companies circumventing the employment ratio of local to foreign workers by offering lower grade jobs to locals and using the quota to recruit foreigners for supervisory jobs; (b) how many companies have been found indulging in such practices in the past five years; and (c) what action has been taken against them.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: To help locals upgrade to better jobs and careers, the Government has put in place various initiatives to improve their skills and help them progress in their job ladders.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: We wish to remind all employers that the Ministry of Manpower (MOM) takes a serious view of all forms of employment discrimination.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: We partner with the Tripartite Alliance for Fair and Progressive Employment Practices (TAFEP) to look into complaints where Singaporeans are not considered fairly for jobs or promotion, at both the rank-and-file and professionals, managers, executives and technicians (PMET) levels.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: Members of the public who are aware of such unfair practices should report them to MOM or TAFEP for investigation.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: TAFEP has been doing important work in ensuring that we address the problem of workplace discrimination, especially when it comes to hiring of foreign workers.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Will the Ministry consider enhancing the capabilities of TAFEP to go beyond promotional work?

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Please wait for my reply at the Committee of Supply (COS).

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: Mr Saktiandi, do you want to wait for the COS?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: In the Minister's experience in dealing with the incidents over the past decade or years, could he share specific industries, for example, that have been flouting some of these rules?

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Whenever we come across employers who may adopt some practices which treat the local workers unfairly as against the foreign workers, TAFEP would take action.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Some would have their application for work pass come under closer scrutiny.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: I would say, on the whole, we do our best as and when we are aware of such unfair practices.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Having said so, I also want to share with the House that we should not jump to the conclusion that simply because the local workers are made to report to foreign workers, the company has done something wrong.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: We have to be mindful that in our workforce today, we have two-thirds local and one-third foreign workforce.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: There are industries where the higher level positions are held mainly by locals.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: And yet, at the production level, a vast majority, 70% to 80% are held by foreign workers.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: In other words, there will be cases where we need the foreign workers to enable us to sustain operations at a higher level, and vice versa.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: There will be areas whereby we do need to create jobs for our rank-and-file workers as well.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Therefore, at MOM, we do not jump to the conclusion whether it is right or wrong when foreign workers are asked to report to local workers, or local workers are asked to report to foreign workers.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: That is where MOM and TAFEP will come in, take it very seriously and take firm action against them.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: As I mentioned earlier, if Members of this House come across any unfair practices based on discrimination, please do not hesitate to alert TAFEP and we will take firm action.
